short: The wartime coalition leader who laid the foundations of the welfare state.
full:
David Lloyd George, a Welsh solicitor, became prime minister in December 1916 after displacing Asquith at the head of a coalition. As chancellor he had introduced old age pensions in 1908 and, through the National Insurance Act of 1911, sickness and unemployment cover; his People's Budget of 1909 provoked the constitutional crisis that stripped the House of Lords of its veto.

In office he reorganised the war effort, forced the convoy system on a reluctant Admiralty, and secured a unified allied command under Foch in 1918. He negotiated at Versailles, extended the franchise to women over thirty, and in December 1921 signed the Anglo-Irish Treaty that created the Irish Free State. The open sale of honours for cash, the brutality of the Black and Tans and Conservative impatience ended the coalition in October 1922. He never held office again, and no Liberal has been prime minister since.
